Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run-chase. The players are back in the middle. Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan make their way out to open for Pakistan. It will be Mehidy Hasan Miraz with the ball for Bangladesh.
…THE RUN CHASE…

Pakistan did well with the ball in the last five overs by picking key wickets and keeping the runs down, but the damage was done in the first half of the innings. The home side gave away too many loose balls and allowed Bangladesh to get a quick start. The spinners were not effective and were taken to the cleaners, but the pace bowlers did a fine job. Hasan Ali and Abbas Afridi, with two each, were the most impressive, while Faheem Ashraf and Shadab Khan chipped in with one apiece. Pakistan will be confident of chasing 197 and making a clean sweep. Can they do it with ease or will  Bangladesh come hard with the ball to defend this total? We shall find out soon. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

A much-improved batting effort from Bangladesh takes them to a solid score of 196/6 from their 20 overs. Having been asked to bat first, Bangladeshi openers started brilliantly and added 110 for the first wicket inside 11 overs to set a good platform. Tanzid Hasan (42) and Parvez Hossain Emon (66) were excellent at the top and took advantage of the field restrictions, along with finding boundaries at will. Both the openers were dismissed in the space of a few overs, post which Litton Das, Tawhid Hridoy, and Jaker Ali struck a few lusty blows for their side to go past the 190-run mark.

A couple of runs to end the innings! Full-length delivery outside off. Jaker Ali drags the slog toward the deep mid-wicket region and charges back for the second. Bangladesh finish on 196/6 from their 20 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: All set now. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan are the openers for Bangladesh. Saim Ayub will start with the ball for Pakistan. Let's play...

Litton Das, the Bangladesh skipper, says that it looks like a good wicket to bat on early. Adds that they did not have any partnerships in the last two games, so want to rectify that. Shares that the last four games haven’t been upto the mark, so want to better that. Mentions that they don’t have any score on mind, but want to start well and think about setting the score later on. Closes by adding that Khaled Mahmud comes in for Shoriful Islam as the only change.

Salman Agha, the Pakistan skipper, wins the toss and opts to bowl. Says that it looks like a good wicket, and wants to use the conditions well. Adds that they want to have six bowling and eight batting options and are happy with the team composition. Shares that they want to continue and are hoping for consistency from the side and wants to keep Bangladesh to an under-par score. Ends by adding that Abbas Afridi comes in for Haris Rauf.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris(WK), Salman Agha(C), Hasan Nawaz, Shadab Khan, Khushdil Shah, Faheem Ashraf, Abbas Afridi (in for Haris Rauf), Hasan Ali, Abrar Ahmed

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das(C)(WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Hasan Mahmud, Khaled Ahmed (in for Shoriful Islam)
Toss Update - Pakistan have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

With Pakistan chasing a whitewash and Bangladesh hoping to restore some pride, the final T20I promises plenty of action. Will the hosts seal a 3-0 sweep, or can Bangladesh strike back to make it 2-1? Stay tuned for the toss and team news coming up shortly!

Bangladesh, for their part, showed some discipline with the ball, especially at the death, thanks to tight spells from Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Hasan Mahmud that prevented Pakistan from pushing beyond 220. However, the batting woes continued. Tanzid Hasan gave them a brisk start, but wickets fell regularly. Only Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Tanzim Sakib offered any resistance in the lower order as the Tigers were bowled out for 144, falling short by 57 runs.

Pakistan, having opted to bat first for the second game in a row, matched their opening T20I total of 201. Sahibzada Farhan and Hasan Nawaz led the charge with explosive fifties, while Mohammad Haris and Salman Agha chipped in with valuable cameos to lift the total past the 200 mark. In response with the ball, Abrar Ahmed impressed with three wickets, while all bowlers, barring Salman Agha, picked up one each, rounding off another comprehensive effort from the home side. Riding high on momentum, the Men in Green will be determined to wrap things up 3-0.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I between Pakistan and Bangladesh, from the iconic Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. With the series already in the bag after two commanding performances, Pakistan will be eyeing a clean sweep. Bangladesh, meanwhile, are playing for pride and will be eager to finish their tour on a high with a consolation win.
…MATCHDAY…

Pakistan will be aiming for a comprehensive 3-0 series whitewash when they take on a struggling Bangladesh side in the third and final T20 International at the Gaddafi Stadium. Having already secured the series with dominant victories in the first two encounters, the hosts are riding high on confidence and will look to cap off the Bangladesh tour of Pakistan, 2025, on a high note. The Green Shirts have been clinical in all departments. In the first T20I, Pakistan posted a formidable 201/7 and comfortably defended it, winning by 37 runs. The second T20I saw a repeat of their batting prowess, as they once again scored 201, this time for the loss of 6 wickets, and restricted Bangladesh to 144 all out, securing a convincing 57-run victory. Under the captaincy of Salman Ali Agha, a new-look Pakistani T20I outfit, featuring a blend of experienced campaigners and promising young talent, has impressed. The decision to rest senior players like Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan, and Shaheen Afridi for this series seems to have paid dividends, allowing others to step up. Sahibzada Farhan has been a revelation at the top, smashing a quick-fire 74 in the second T20I. Mohammad Haris has also shown aggressive intent, contributing significantly in the middle order. The likes of Saim Ayub and Hasan Nawaz have also chipped in with crucial performances. The bowling attack, led by stalwarts like Haris Rauf and Hasan Ali, and supported by the spin of Abrar Ahmed and Shadab Khan, has consistently troubled the Bangladeshi batsmen. Fakhar Zaman, who missed the second game due to fitness issues, might return for the final match, further strengthening the batting lineup. For Bangladesh, led by Litton Das, the series has been a tough learning experience. Their batting has failed to fire collectively against a disciplined Pakistani attack. While there have been glimpses of individual brilliance, they haven't been able to build substantial partnerships or chase down daunting totals. Key players like Najmul Hossain Shanto, Tawhid Hridoy, and Litton Das himself will need to shoulder more responsibility if Bangladesh hopes to salvage some pride in the final game. Historically, Pakistan has held a significant advantage over Bangladesh in T20Is. Out of the 20 matches played between the two sides, Pakistan has won 17, while Bangladesh has managed only 3 victories. At the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, Pakistan's record against Bangladesh is even more imposing, having won all three encounters played there prior to this ongoing match. The pitch at the Gaddafi Stadium has generally been good for batting, as evidenced by Pakistan's consecutive 200+ scores in the series. However, it also offers assistance to both pacers and spinners who are willing to hit the right areas. Who do you think will come out on top?
